SC = State-Controlled, ISFM = Independent State-Funded and State-Managed. Information checked to 30 September 2026.

Corporación de Radio y Televisión Española, S.A. is Spain’s state-owned public-service broadcaster. It was constituted on 12 September 2006 and began operating on 1 January 2007, succeeding the former RTVE public body and its television and radio companies. The state owns its entire share capital through the Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales, SEPI. José Pablo López has been President since 2 December 2024.

Media assets

RTVE’s 2025 corporate report identifies these principal services:

Television in Spain: La 1, La 2, Canal 24h, Teledeporte and Clan. RTVE also transmits La 1 in ultra-high definition. La2Cat, launched in October 2025, provides a predominantly Catalan-language service in Catalonia.

International television: TVE Internacional and Star HD

Radio: Radio Nacional, Radio Clásica, Radio 3, Ràdio 4, Radio 5 and Radio Exterior de España

Digital: rtve.es, RTVE Play and RNE Audio

Ownership and governance

RTVE is wholly state-owned, but Law 17/2006 gives it legal autonomy and requires it to act independently of the government in carrying out its functions. Its Board and President are chosen through parliamentary procedures.

Royal Decree-Law 5/2024 expanded the Board from 10 to 15 members: 11 elected by the Congress of Deputies and four by the Senate. Members serve six-year terms and have exclusive, full-time dedication.

A two-thirds majority remains required on the first ballot; if it is not obtained, an absolute majority can elect members on a second ballot at least 48 hours later. The second-ballot route had appeared in temporary arrangements in 2018; the 2024 reform incorporated it into the regular procedure. The reform also transferred some ordinary executive powers from the Board to its President.

Congress elected 11 members on 14 November 2024, and the Senate elected four on 21 November, both in second-round votes. Congress elected José Pablo López President on 28 November with 178 votes; he and the other members took office on 2 December. Concepción Cascajosa had served as interim President from March 2024.

RTVE has an existing Mandato-Marco, approved in December 2007 and effective from January 2008. RTVE’s 2025 accounts state that it remains extended pending a replacement and that the associated Contratos-Programa had not been signed. A parliamentary subcommittee was working on a new mandate in September 2026.

Source of funding and budget

Ordinary domestic commercial advertising ended under Law 8/2009, although the law permits specified sponsorship, international commercial communication and digital exploitation.

RTVE receives public-service compensation through the state budget, an allocation linked to the radio-spectrum reservation fee, statutory contributions from audiovisual businesses and other income. Current law fixes the spectrum allocation at EUR 480 million annually unless a budget law sets another amount. It does not use an “80 per cent of fee revenue” formula. The contribution rates are 3 per cent for qualifying free-to-air television services and 1.5 per cent for qualifying pay television, on-demand and video-sharing services, subject to the law’s definitions and limits.

The figure of EUR 1.1819 billion previously cited for 2024 is the accounts’ total for recognised grants and related contributions, not its approved total budget. The regulator CNMC records a 2024 income budget of EUR 1.2697 billion and an expenditure budget of EUR 1.2997 billion. A comparable, independently verified 2026 approved-budget figure was not established for this update; full-year 2026 accounts are not yet due.

Editorial independence

Law 17/2006 contains specific provisions. It requires functional independence from government, plural and objective information, and protection of journalists’ professional independence. Its statutory News Councils may examine editorial policy, raise concerns and issue non-binding opinions on proposed news-director appointments. RTVE also has an information statute, a published style manual, an audience ombudsperson, parliamentary scrutiny and external supervision by CNMC.

Concerns about influence remain substantial. The European Commission’s 2026 Rule of Law Report records stakeholders’ concerns about the 2024 governance reform and cites a January 2026 report by the TVE and RNE News Councils alleging declining professional standards and perceived political bias.

TVE’s News Council report ran to 144 pages, following more than 100 staff complaints, alleging repeated breaches of journalistic standards and political bias in Mañaneros 360 and Malas lenguas. RTVE’s management and Board disputed its findings and methodology.

In its assessment of 2024 TVE news, CNMC found that government members and supporting parties received 50.20 per cent of recorded speaking time, against 49.80 per cent for opposition parties, describing that aggregate division as close to balanced while warning that balance could differ by party, programme and audience period. For the first quarter of 2026, RTVE’s account of CNMC data reports 53.03 per cent for the government bloc and 46.97 per cent for the opposition. CNMC’s wider findings for the same quarter were markedly less even. The government bloc received 68.24 per cent of measured speaking time in Informe Semanal, across five programmes, and 66.46 per cent in RNE news, against 31.76 and 33.54 per cent respectively for the opposition. Speaking-time shares do not measure story selection, tone or government instructions to editors, and the 2024 figures largely precede the present Board.

A September 2026 dispute provides more recent evidence of tension inside the newsroom. TVE’s News Council objected when management asked that its criticism of a prime-ministerial interview be omitted from one Telediario report; journalists protested. RTVE’s presidency denied ideological censorship, saying the request concerned editorial coordination and that the Council’s criticism had appeared elsewhere on RTVE.

AI and digital policy

RTVE has documented internal AI rules. Its Board approved a general AI-use standard in September 2024, covering responsible use by staff and suppliers; its 2025 report describes the provisions of Norma 1/2024. In March 2026 RTVE said it was developing additional guidance specifically for news services. The full text of a publicly accessible newsroom-specific policy was not independently identified.

Classification rationale

RTVE is classified Independent State-Funded and State-Managed (ISFM), provisionally. This September 2026 review moves it from State-Controlled (SC).

The state owns RTVE through SEPI. Parliament elects its 15-member Board, and public-service compensation and the statutory radio-spectrum allocation provide most of its funding. These arrangements create substantial opportunities for political influence over governance.

The change in classification rests on the editorial criterion. Law 17/2006 requires functional independence from government and establishes News Councils to defend journalists’ independence and scrutinise news output. CNMC found the aggregate speaking time of the government bloc and opposition in TVE news close to even in 2024, and RTVE reported a similarly close division in CNMC’s first-quarter 2026 figures. CNMC’s wider first-quarter 2026 findings were less even, with the government bloc at 68.24 per cent in Informe Semanal and 66.46 per cent in RNE news. These measures cover speaking time in specified programmes, not story selection, tone or government instructions to editors. The evidence reviewed for this update does not establish a sustained pattern of editorial decisions imposed or approved by the government.

The classification remains provisional because the editorial concerns are substantial. The 2024 Board reform permits election by an absolute majority on a second ballot. In 2026 the News Councils raised concerns about professional standards and perceived political bias; TVE’s Council investigated two programmes in detail, and journalists challenged a management decision affecting a September Telediario report. RTVE disputed the Council’s programme findings and denied ideological censorship in the September case. The European Commission records these concerns. These findings justify continued scrutiny without, by themselves, satisfying the test for state editorial control.

The next review should examine comparable content across RTVE’s news and current-affairs services under the present Board, the resolution of the News Councils’ findings, and any documented instructions from political authorities concerning coverage. The earlier monitoring from 2023 and 2024 should be dated and described as evidence from the preceding leadership period.
